questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Hema doesn't has (1)/ to give (2)/ the dissertation to me. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 1**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **According to the rule, **the auxiliary verb **'do/does/did'** is always followed by the **main verb,** and the main verb should be in **V₁** form. 
 
• Let's see an example:
 
 
• He **doesn't spend** time with me.* (does is an auxiliary verb and spend (V₁) is the main verb.)*
 
 
 
• ​**Have **is an irregular verb. Its three forms are **'have, had, had'.** &

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

My mother (1)/ has (2)/ grey hairs. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The word **‘hair’ **is generally an* ***uncountable noun**.
 
• An uncountable noun is generally not followed by **'s' **at the end.
 
 
• For instance: I dyed my* *hair black. (a mass of hair is being dyed)
 
 
 
• Hence, the error is in the third part of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: *My mother has grey **hair**.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some parts of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Oh dear, (1)/ do have some relief (2)/ on my nerves (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
In the given sentence **Part 2** has an error in it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The word, **‘relief’ **which refers to a** feeling of reassurance following release from anxiety or distress**, seems* incorrect *in the given context.
 
• Here, the person should be asking for ‘pity/concern’ on/for his nerves and not ‘relief’.
 
• **'Have pity on'** is a phrase which means **'To act compassionately or with sympathy toward one'.**
 
• **Examples: **
 
 
• *Please, have pity on me, I don't want to die!*
 
• *The three spirits taught Scrooge how to have pity on his fellow man.*

 

 
 
 

**Correct sentence: ***Oh dear, do have some **pity** on my nerves.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Once you graduate, (1)/ get a job (2)/ would be easier (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The error is in part 2 of the sentence.

The *incorrect form *of the verb *‘get’* is used. To correct the sentence, **‘ing’** should be added to ‘get’. Also, we can see that the word,** ‘getting’ **won’t be acting as a verb, but as a noun, i.e. it is a **gerund**.

Here, the speaker is talking about how* getting a job *would be easier after graduation; where ‘getting’ acts as a noun, while ‘would’ is the verb.

questions.question:

He has been (1)/ working here (2)/ for quite some time (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The given sentence has no error.

In the first part of the sentence, the *verb agrees with the subject*, and there’s no grammatical error in the rest of the sentence, hence, 4 is the solution.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

I decided (1)/ to climbed to the (2)/ top of the hill (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The error is in part 2 of the sentence.

The *incorrect form* of the verb, ‘climb’ is used in combination with ‘to’. The* bare infinitive* form of the verb, (i.e., ‘**climb**’), should be used; here, ‘**to climb**’ is the correct usage and not ‘to climbed’.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Reading (1)/ provides nutrition (2)/ with the mind (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The error lies in part 3 of the sentence.

Here, an incorrect preposition, ’**with**’ is used.

The correct preposition should ‘**identify the affected thing (i.e., mind)**’. This function can be fulfilled by ‘**to**’, but, *not* by ‘**with**’.

Nutrition is provided ***to*** the mind,* not*, ***with*** the mind.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Despite of minimal use of technology (1)/ they are able to manage (2)/ everything in a simple manner (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The error is in part 1 of the sentence.

There is an *unnecessary preposition* in part 1. The word, ‘**despite**’, which has the meaning ‘**in spite of**’, doesn’t need the support of any preposition, so, ‘**of**’, should be eliminated.

The correct phrase would be: ‘*Despite* minimal use of technology’.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Sri Lanka is an island country (1) / into the Indian Ocean (2)/, south of India. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The error is in part 2 of the sentence.

An incorrect preposition, ‘***into***’ is used. The word, ‘**in**’ which ‘**expresses the situation of something that is surrounded/ enclosed by something else**’ would be more appropriate.

Sri Lanka is*** *in** the Indian Ocean.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

I'm content with what I make (1)/ and I am found simple joy in seeing a smile on the customer's face (2)/ when they smell the jasmine flowers. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The sentence is clearly incorrect because part 2 of the sentence is not error-free.

‘I *am found *simple joy in seeing a smile on the customer’s face’ is wrong, because of the incorrect tense form. ‘**I *have found* simple joy...**’ would be more appropriate.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Each item was sold ________ a pound.
questions.solution: The missing word should be a preposition, which has the meaning ‘**charged as (a price)**’. The word, ‘**for**’ has the required meaning, and is the solution.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Be just ________ fear nothing.
questions.solution:
The missing word is the conjunction, ‘**and**’.

This is because, ‘*being just and being fearless’* are two very different things, which can be connected only by ‘and’.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

He came two hours ________ us.
questions.solution:
The missing word should be a *preposition*, which can be followed by an object (or, a particular event). This can only be done by ‘**before**’.

*Ago* can’t be followed by an object.

*Above* isn’t generally used in cases of time.

*Ahead* will always be followed by a preposition like ‘of’.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Sunaina said, "She is sick ________ the whole business."
questions.solution: The missing word should be a *preposition*. In this context, the phrase, ‘**sick of**’ has the meaning ‘**intensely annoyed with, or bored by**’, so the missing word is ‘***of***’.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

He was quite ________ when he heard what had happened.
questions.solution:
The missing word should be an adjective. The word ‘**amused**’ refers to ‘**finding something funny or entertaining**’, which quite fits the context.

The words, ‘laughing’, ‘lovable’ and ‘beautiful’ aren’t quite relevant, in spite of being adjectives.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

We saw you and him.

options.text: You and he were seen by us.
He and you were seen by us.
You were seen by us with him.
Both of you were seen by us.

questions.solution:
When we change a sentence in the active voice to passive, we know that the subject will become the object, and the object will become the subject.

Here, ‘**You and he**’ becomes the main subject, the verb changes to ‘**were seen by**’ and the object is ‘**us**’.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

Tom painted the entire house.

options.text: The entire house was painted by Tom.
The entire house is painted by Tom.
The entire house were painted by Tom.
The house is painted by Tom.

questions.solution: In passive voice, the verb changes according to the tense. Here, ‘**painted**’ should become ‘**was painted**’, since all the other options have incorrect tense forms, Option 1 is correct.

questions.question:
**sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

The science class viewed the comet.

options.text: The comet was viewed by the science class.
The comet is been viewed by the science class.
The comet is viewed by the science class.

questions.solution: According to the rules, the verb must be changed, but not the tense- ‘**was viewed**’ is the required change. Hence, Option 2 is correct.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

The kangaroo carried her baby in her pouch.

options.text: The baby was carried by the kangaroo in her pouch.
The kangaroo carried the baby in pouch.
The baby is carried by kangaroo in her pouch
The baby is being carried up by kangaroo in her pouch.

questions.solution: The verb ‘**carried**’ must be changed to ‘**was carried**’ when converting to Passive voice. Since, all the other options fail to follow these rules of conversion, Option 1 is correct.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

Grandma is knitting the sweater.

options.text: The sweater is being knit by grandma.
The sweater was being knit by grandma.

questions.solution: According to the rules, the verb must be changed to ‘**is being knit**’. This rule is followed only by Option 1, so it is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

Who teaches you English?

options.text: Do you know who teaches you English?
By whom are you taught English?

questions.solution:
According to the rules:- ‘Teaches’ will change to ‘**are taught**’, and ‘who’ will change to ‘**by whom**’.

These rules are followed only in Option 3, so, it is the solution.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

Mohita was weaving the basket.

options.text: The basket was woven by Mohita
The basket is woven by Mohita
The basket is being woven by Mohita
The basket was being woven by Mohita

questions.solution:
In the given sentence, the past continuous tense form of the verb is used, so we must be careful when we convert the voice.

‘**Was weaving**’ changes to ‘**was being woven**’. And, the subject and object switch places.

So, Option 4 is correct.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

The hunter shot the deer.

options.text: The deer is shot by the hunter
The deer was shot by the hunter
The hunter was shot by the deer

questions.solution: ‘**Shot**’ is in simple past tense, so when we change to passive voice, it becomes ‘**was shot**’. Also, the subject and the object switch places.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

Rohan gave the work to Pooja.

options.text: The work has given to Pooja by Rohan
The work is given to Pooja by Rohan.
The work was given to Pooja by Rohan
The work will be given to Pooja by Rohan.

questions.solution:
In the given sentence, there are two objects- a direct object (**the work**) and an indirect object (**Pooja**). Either of them can be made the main subject; here, ‘the work’ is the subject.

Also, the verb, ‘gave’ which is in simple past must be changed to ‘**was given**’. But, only Option 3 follows all the rules of conversion, hence, it is the solution.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

Mrs. Sharma invited us to her house party.

options.text: We were invited by Mrs. Sharma to her house party.
We are invited by Mrs. Sharma for house party.
We will be invited by Mrs. Sharma for house party.
We are invited for the house party by Mrs. Sharma.

questions.solution:
The object ‘**us**’ must be changed to ‘**we**’, since it is a subject and not an object anymore.

The verb ‘**invited**’ must be changed to ‘**were invited**’, because of the Active-Passive rule and for Subject-Verb agreement.

These rules are only followed in Option 1 hence, it is the correct answer.

questions.question:

Among the given words,

‘Similar’ means *‘Resembling in appearance’*

‘Vague’ means *’Indefinite/ Unclear character’*

Since, none of these words has the required meaning, (in fact they are quite antonymous), Option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:

Condemn
questions.solution:
The word, ‘condemn’ refers to ’**expressing disapproval**’.

Three of the words- Approve, Laud and, Commend- are antonymous in meaning to ‘condemn’, so Option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word.**

‘Dingy’ means ‘**gloomy and dull**’.

The meaning of the words,

*Pure*: Clear/ Clean

Clear: Easy to understand

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word.**

Constant
questions.solution:
The word, ‘Constant’ refers to ‘**something that does not change**’.

Three of the options are about change/ movement, so they can all be eliminated; the correct answer is ‘fixed’, which has the required meaning.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word.**

Confine
questions.solution:
The word ‘confine’ is a *verb* that refers to ‘**the act of keeping or restricting someone within certain limits**’.

Among the given words, 3 of them- ‘Restrain, Restrict, Imprison’ are quite *synonymous* to ‘confine’, so, Option 1 which means ‘**to officially allow or authorize**’ is the solution.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word.**

Defeat
questions.solution:
The word, ‘Defeat’ is a noun, which has the meaning ‘**an instance of being overcome/ beaten/ defeated**’.

Among the given words, 3 of them- ‘Beat, Collapse, Loss’ are quite *synonymous* to ‘Defeat’ , so, Option 2 which refers to ‘**the action of achieving a goal**’ is the solution.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word.**

Fervent
questions.solution:
The word, ’Fervent’ is an adjective, refers to ‘**a display of passionate intensity**’.

Among the given words, 3 of them- ‘Passionate, Zealous, Blazing’ are quite synonymous to ‘Fervent’, so, Option 2 which has the meaning ‘**Unemotional**’ is the solution.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word.**

Imitation
questions.solution:
The word,’Imitation’ is a noun that refers to ‘**a thing intended to simulate something else**’.

Among the given words, 2 of them- ‘Copy and, Echo’ is quite synonymous to ‘Imitation’, while ‘Follow’ means ‘to travel behind’. So, Option 3 which has the meaning ‘**Genuine**’ is the solution.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word.**

Immense
questions.solution:
The word,’immense’ has the meaning ‘**extremely large or great**’.

Among the given words, 3 of them- ‘BIg, Huge and Grand’ are *synonymous* with ‘Immense’, so, Option 2 which has the meaning ‘**very small**’ is the solution.

questions.question:

Apple of one's eye

An example in a sentence would be: I’ve given them a list of changes that I think are necessary, so, the *ball is in their court *now.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.**

Last straw

options.text: Last problem in the series of problems

questions.solution:
The correct answer is- '**Last problem in the series of problems**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's understand the meaning of the given idiom:
 
• '**Last straw**' means the last in a series of unpleasant events that finally makes you feel that you cannot continue to accept a bad situation

 Example: *She's always been rude to me, but it was **the last straw** when she started insulting my mother.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's learn about the origin of the idiom:
 
 
• *The origin of the idiom 'the last straw' can be found in the old English proverb, “it is the last straw that breaks the camel’s back.” It was first seen around 1755, and many different forms of the statement were used between then and about 1836, with the suffering animal occasionally described as a horse or an elephant rather than as a camel.*

questions.question:
**Improve the bold part of the sentence:**

**(The bundle of coins were the only source)** of information for them.

options.text: The bundles of coins were the only source.
The bundles of coins were the only sources.
The bundle of coins was the only source.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The bundle of coins was the only source**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A noun is a word that names a person, place, thing, idea, etc.
 
• A collective noun refers to a group of people or things. 
 
 
• Example: a herd of cows, a bundle of sticks, a bunch of keys, a team of players, etc.
 
 
 
• A collective noun takes a singular verb. 
 
 
• Example: The team has left for its tour of Australia.
 
 
 
• So, 'were' should be replaced with 'was' in the sentence.

Correct sentence__: *The bundle of coins was the only source** of information for them.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• If there is a division or difference of opinion among the members of the collective noun, we use plural verb and plural pronoun.

 
 
• Example: The audience have taken their seats.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

No sooner **(do the phone ring)**, he was out of the home.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__did the phone ring__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• No sooner is used to show that one thing happens immediately after another thing. It is often used with the past perfect or simple past and usually followed by 'than'.
 
• The preposition 'than' is used in expressions indicating one thing happening immediately after another.
 
• When a sentence begins with negative adverbs like Hardly, scarcely, no sooner, etc inversion of the sentence takes place. In such a case helping verb should come before the main verb.
 
• **'did' **is always followed by the **V₁ form of the verb.**

**​The correct sentence is: ***No sooner **did the phone ring**, he was out of the home.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

Two more employees **(will be hiring)** by the company.
questions.solution:
The sentence is clearly in* passive voice*, as the *doer of the action*- ‘**company**’ is an object.

Also, the tense is future.

Hence, ‘**will hire**’ changes to ‘**will be hired**’. So, the solution is Option 2.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

This **(modern furnitures will be sold)** in the main market.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '__**modern furniture will be sold**__'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the use of the plural form of the noun 'furnitures' is incorrect.
 
• The noun ''furniture'' is acting as an uncountable noun in the sentence.
 
• The uncountable nouns have a singular form and do not have a plural form i.e. we can't add an 's' to it.
 
• Therefore, the singular form of the noun 'furniture' should be used in place of the plural noun 'furnitures'.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct Sentence: *This modern furniture will be sold in the main market.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

My boss **(have being given**) me a lot of work.
questions.solution:
The given sentence requires improvement, since, there is **no subject-verb agreement**.

Additionally, the tense is incorrect- it should be **present perfect continuous**.

These rules are followed only by Option 3.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

I **(wander about)** the stars up in the sky.
questions.solution: ‘To wander’ means ‘to roam’, but ‘*roaming about the stars*’ makes very little sense. On the other hand, ‘**wondering/feeling curious about the stars**’ seems correct, hence, Option 2 is correct.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

Go right and **(keep a sharp left turn)** you will reach the place.
questions.solution:
The verb, ’keep’ seems incorrect in the given sentence.

‘Take a sharp left turn’ makes more sense, hence, Option 1 is correct.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

Heena **(keep a eye)** on his son.
questions.solution:
We know that the word, ‘*eye*’ will take the article, ‘**an**’, as it is *singular* and begins with a *vowel*. So, we can eliminate the original sentence and options 1 and 4 as well.

This leaves us with 2 and 3, of which, 2 is incorrect, since, there’s* no subject-verb agreement*.

The correct usage is ‘to keep an eye on’ which has the meaning ‘to watch someone or something carefully’

Hence, 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

options.text: She enquired at what time the train arrived.

She said when does the train arrive.

questions.solution:
For questions which can’t be answered with a yes or no, we generally place the question word after the reporting verb and then change the question to an *assertive form* with the necessary *tense change*.

Here, ‘**what time does the train arrive**’ changes to ‘**at what time the train arrived**’.

All the other options are incorrect.

questions.question:

questions.solution:
According to the rules, since, the reporting verb is in simple past, the reported speech must change tense.

Here, the word, ’must’ changes to ‘**had to**’; i.e. the correct sentence would be: He said that he had to work hard.

questions.question:

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

He said to Rama, "Come with me."

options.text: He asked Rama to go with him.
He pleaded Rama to go with him.
He said Rama to come with him.
Rama come with me he said.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'He asked Rama to go with him.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When converting a direct command or request to indirect speech, the verb often changes to a form of 'ask' to convey the request or command indirectly.
 
• The original sentence, "Come with me," is a command or request, making 'asked' the appropriate verb for the indirect speech.
 
• The pronoun "me" in direct speech becomes "him" in indirect speech to match the speaker's perspective.
 
• There is no indication in the original sentence of the tone being a plea; it is simply a request or command, making 'asked' the most neutral and accurate choice.
 
• The structure of the indirect speech correctly orders the subject ("He"), followed by the verb indicating action ("asked"), and then the object of the action ("Rama") along with the request made ("to go with him").

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 2 ('He pleaded Rama to go with him.') introduces a tone of pleading that was not specified in the original statement.
 
• Option 3 ('He said Rama to come with him.') is grammatically incorrect in the context of reporting speech; "said to" is used in direct speech, but in indirect speech, the structure changes.
 
• Option 4 ('Rama come with me he said.') is a direct speech format without proper punctuation and does not correctly convert the sentence into indirect speech.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

The boxes

P-were heavy

Q-so carrying two of them

R-was a lot of weight to handle
questions.solution:
The first phrase must begin with the plural verb, ‘**were**’, since, ‘boxes’ is a plural noun. So, **P** is first.

The third phrase, **R** begins with ‘*was*’, because it is the predicate part of the subject- ‘carrying two of them’ in Q.

The order is PQR.

questions.question:
